ali: Thanks for the AH update. Quick ask: we're seeing a spike in infra costs for eval clusters. Before we open tickets, want to clarify thresholds for auto-approvals vs formal intake.

rita: We're seeing daily spikes due to longer eval runs. If we need temporary capacity for 2-3 weeks, can we use P-card or do we need a PO?

maria (CFO): Temporary capacity under $5k total is fine on P-card if manager approves. >$5k & < $20k route through Finance Ops for expedited review; >$20k requires full Procurement intake. For anything that looks repeatable, we want a committed plan (Dedicated) instead of continuing ad-hoc spend.

dylan (Finance Ops): For expedited reviews, include expected duration, peak TPS/GCUs, and whether caching/burst options were considered. We can often approve short-term credits or cloud cost controls in 24hrs.

infra-oncall: If we submit an expedited review, will we get usage caps applied automatically?

dylan (Finance Ops): We can apply temporary spend caps and set alerts. Include requested cap in the form.

rita: good to know. Any guidance about tagging cost to projects for chargebacks?

maria (CFO): Always tag infra spend with the project code. If it's an eval for a customer, use the customer code and note it's externally funded in the form; that can change approval path.

sam (CEO): Operational note: if a 2-3 week burst enables a critical demo/won deal, prioritize velocity but try to minimize runway impact. Finance will support high-ROI short bursts.

ali: Action items: 1) infra to try burst configs and autoscaling before opening ticket; 2) if still needed, use FIN-310 expedited form; 3) finance will target 24hr response for < $20k cases.

procure-bot: Created FIN-310-2: "2-week eval cluster burst request" and assigned to dylan.

rita: Thanks team 44d

dylan (Finance Ops): If anyone's unclear about thresholds, DM me or ping finance-ops channel.

maria (CFO): Also: we'll publish a short decision tree in the docs page later today.

ali: great, thanks everyone.
